# Tobit Chapter 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_006_page_001.jpg

---

**6:1** They set out on their way, the dog running along with them, and they spent the first night at the river Tigris.

**6:2** When the young man went down to the river to wash his feet, a large fish leaped from the water and tried to swallow his foot. He cried out in alarm.

**6:3** The angel said to him, "Grab hold of the fish!" The young man seized it and dragged it up onto the bank.

**6:4** The angel said to him, "Cut open the fish and take out its heart, liver, and gall, and keep these with you carefully."

**6:5** The young man did as the angel had commanded him. He cut open the fish, took out the heart, liver, and gall, and set them aside. He roasted some of the fish and ate it; the rest he salted and kept for the journey.

Then the two of them traveled on together until they were drawing near to Media.

**6:6** The young man asked the angel: "Brother Azariah, what is the heart and the liver and the gall of the fish good for? What healing use do these things have?"

**6:7** He said, "As for the heart and liver — if any person is tormented by a demon or an evil spirit, one must make a smoke from these before that person, and he will be freed from all torment forever.

**6:8** As for the gall — smear it on the eyes of a man who has white films over his eyes, and he will be healed."

**6:9** When they were drawing near to Media and already approaching Ecbatana,

**6:10** Raphael said to the young man Tobias, "Brother Tobias." He answered, "Here I am." Raphael said, "Tonight we must lodge with Raguel, who is a kinsman of yours. He has a daughter named Sarah.

**6:11** He has no other son or daughter except Sarah alone, and you are his nearest heir — all his possessions will come to you. The girl is sensible, courageous, and very beautiful, and her father is a good man.

**6:12** You have the right to take her as your wife. So hear me, brother, and tonight I will speak to her father about the girl, that she may be given to you as your bride. And when we return from Rages, we will celebrate the wedding. For I know that Raguel cannot refuse her to you or betroth her to another man — that would bring death upon him according to the ordinance in the book of Moses, seeing that you are her rightful heir. So listen, brother, and tonight we will speak to her father about the girl and ask her hand for you."

**6:13** Tobias answered Raphael: "Brother Azariah, I have heard that this girl has been given to seven men, and every one of them died in the bridal chamber on the night he went in to her. I am told that a demon kills them.

**6:14** I am afraid, because the demon does nothing to her but kills every man who tries to approach her. I am my father's only child. If I die, I will bring my father and mother down in grief to their grave, and they have no other son to bury them."

**6:15** The angel said to him, "Have you not remembered your father's commandment to take a wife from your own kindred? Now hear me, brother, and give this demon no thought. Take her.

**6:16** I know that tonight she will be given to you as your wife.

**6:17** When you enter the bridal chamber, take the heart and liver from the fish organs and place them on the smoldering incense coals, and the smoke will spread —

**6:18** and the demon will smell it and flee and never return again. Then, before you come together with her, both of you rise and pray; petition the Lord of heaven to grant you mercy and protection. Do not be afraid, for she was appointed for you before the ages. You will deliver her, and she will go with you. And I believe you will have children by her. Do not be troubled."

When Tobias heard the words of Raphael — and understood that Sarah was his kinswoman, from his father's own house — he loved her deeply, and his heart clung to her.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agreed on preserving "white films" or equivalent for *leukōmata* (the reader already knows from ch. 2 that this describes Tobit's blindness, so no gloss is needed). All three retained the "before the ages" predestination language at v. 18. The Genesis 2:24 echo in the final verse ("his heart clung to her") was recognized and honored by all three, though PNEUMA expanded it most fully.

---
## Disagreement Log

| Verse | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA's Resolution |
|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------------|
| 6:1 | "he-lodged the-first night at-the river Tigris" | "they spent the first night camped at the river Tigris" | "spent their first night camped beside the Tigris" | LOGOS — natural English, retains "Tigris" in full |
| 6:2 | "sought to-devour the-foot of-the-young-man" | "tried to swallow his foot" | "snapped at his foot" | LOGOS — "swallow" better renders *katapein* (gulp down) than PNEUMA's "snap" |
| 6:3 | "drew-it up onto-the land" | "hauled it up onto the bank" | "wrestled it up onto the bank" | LOGOS — "dragged" chosen as midpoint; PNEUMA's "wrestled" adds drama not in the Greek |
| 6:4 | "bile" | "gall" | "gall" | LOGOS/PNEUMA — "gall" is the standard English term for *cholē* in the Hebrew Bible tradition |
| 6:5 | "gathered together its-heart and its-liver and its-bile" | "removed the heart, liver, and gall" | "took out the organs" | LOGOS — complete and clear; PNEUMA's "organs" is too general |
| 6:7 | "smoke these [before] him" | "make a smoke from these before that person" | "you burn the heart and liver as smoke before them" | LOGOS — "make a smoke from these" is most precise for the fumigation ritual |
| 6:8 | "whiteness in-his-eyes" | "white films over his eyes" | "where they've gone white" | LOGOS — "white films" is both medically clear and faithful to *leukōmata* |
| 6:11 | "sensible, courageous, and very-beautiful" | "sensible, courageous, and very beautiful" | "sensible and brave and very beautiful" | LOGOS — "courageous" preferred to PNEUMA's "brave" for the more formal register |
| 6:14 | "bring my-father and my-mother down to-their-grave with-grief over-me" | "bring my father and mother down in grief to their grave" | "it will kill my parents too — they'll die of grief" | LOGOS — preserves the Semitic idiom (cf. Gen 42:38) without PNEUMA's expansion |
| 6:18 | "assigned to-you from before-the-age" | "appointed for you before the ages" | "made for you before the beginning of time" | LOGOS — "appointed for you before the ages" is precise and appropriately elevated |
| Final verse | "his heart was-clinging to-her" | "his heart clung to her" | "His heart held fast to her, and would not let go" | LOGOS — "his heart clung to her" preserves the Genesis echo cleanly; PNEUMA's expansion is moving but adds words not in the Greek |
